findings.title: Fallbacks module included into wrong backend class, breaking I18n fallback behavior
findings.body: The initializer does `I18n.backend.class.send(:include, I18n::Backend::Fallbacks)`. At initializer time, `I18n.backend` is an instance of `I18n::Backend::Simple` (the default backend), so this includes Fallbacks into `I18n::Backend::Simple` itself. However, the translate_accelerator freedom patch reopens `I18n::Backend::Simple` and the app's actual translation path goes through the patched `I18n.translate` which calls `translate_no_cache` (the original `I18n.translate`). The Fallbacks module works by overriding `translate` on the backend to walk the fallback chain; including it into the backend class does not make `I18n::Backend::Simple#translate` perform fallback lookups unless the backend's `translate` is the Fallbacks-aware one. More importantly, `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` must be included into the backend *instance's* class and it expects `I18n.fallbacks` to respond to `[](locale)` returning an array — which `FallbackLocaleList` does — but the standard, supported way is `I18n::Backend::Simple.send(:include, I18n::Backend::Fallbacks)` combined with `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` (which the PR removes from all environment configs). The consequence: users with partially-translated locales see raw 'translation missing: xx.key' messages in the UI. The fix is to keep `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` in the environment configs (or set `I18n::Backend::Simple.send(:include, I18n::Backend::Fallbacks)` and ensure the fallbacks config flag is set), and include Fallbacks into `I18n::Backend::Simple` (the class), not `I18n.backend.class` (which is fragile and equivalent only by accident at boot).
